# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey tools that help businesses and individuals collect data from their audience. This comparison is beneficial for those looking to switch from a proprietary solution like Typeform to a self-hosted, open-source alternative like Formbricks, particularly if data ownership and cost are key concerns.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Formbricks is free and self-hosted, while Typeform has a subscription-based model.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to have full control over their data, whereas Typeform stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Typeform has a more user-friendly interface and easier setup, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be more scalable due to its self-hosted nature, while Typeform has limitations on the number of responses and users.
* Integration: Typeform has a more extensive library of integrations with third-party tools, while Formbricks has limited integrations but can be customized using its open-source code.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $25-$40/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $83-$125/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Typeform:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party tools
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data
* Can be expensive for large teams
**Formbricks:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full control over data
* Customizable using open-source code
* Limited integrations with third-party tools
* Requires technical expertise to set up

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that need a user-friendly interface and a wide range of integrations with third-party tools. It's also suitable for those who don't mind paying a subscription fee and don't require full control over their data. On the other hand, Formbricks is ideal for larger teams or organizations that require full control over their data and are comfortable with self-hosting and customizing their solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Formbricks instance on your server.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to migrate your data from the exported CSV or JSON file.
4. Customize your Formbricks instance to fit your needs.
5. Test your forms and surveys to ensure they are working as expected.

## Our Take
Formbricks is still a relatively new solution, and while it shows promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Formbricks requires a good understanding of server management and customization. However, for teams that value data ownership and customization, Formbricks is definitely worth considering, and we recommend switching if you have the technical expertise and resources to support it.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with limited budget and no need for advanced integrations
* Medium-sized teams that require full control over their data
* Large organizations with in-house technical expertise
* Teams that don't need advanced customer support
* Developers who want to customize their form and survey solution using open-source code

## FAQ
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is free and self-hosted, which means you can use it at no cost, but you'll need to cover server costs.
### Is Formbricks compatible with all browsers?
Formbricks is compatible with most modern browsers, but it may not work perfectly with older browsers.
### Can I integrate Formbricks with third-party tools?
Formbricks has limited integrations with third-party tools, but it can be customized using its open-source code.
### Is Formbricks suitable for large teams?
Formbricks can be suitable for large teams, but it requires technical expertise to set up and customize.
### Can I export my data from Formbricks?
Yes, you can export your data from Formbricks in CSV or JSON format.

# Miro vs Excalidraw (2026)

## Overview
Miro and Excalidraw are two popular tools used for collaborative whiteboarding and visual project management. Both tools cater to teams and individuals looking to streamline their workflow, brainstorm ideas, and work together on projects. The key reason someone would switch from Miro to Excalidraw is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs, as Excalidraw offers a free, self-hosted option.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Miro offers a free plan, as well as paid plans starting at $8-$16 per user per month, while Excalidraw is free with optional self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Excalidraw allows users to self-host their data, giving them full control and ownership, whereas Miro stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Excalidraw requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, whereas Miro offers a more straightforward, cloud-based solution.
* Scalability: Miro is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while Excalidraw may require more manual configuration to support very large teams.
* Integration with other tools: Miro offers a wider range of integrations with popular tools like Google Drive, Trello, and Slack, whereas Excalidraw has more limited integration options.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400-$800/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600-$3,200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Miro:**
* Pros:
	+ Easy to use and set up
	+ Wide range of integrations with other tools
	+ Scalable for large teams and enterprises
	+ Offers a free plan
	+ Good customer support
* Cons:
	+ Limited control over data ownership
	+ Can be expensive for large teams
	+ Limited customization options
**Excalidraw:**
* Pros:
	+ Free and open-source
	+ Self-hosting option for full data control
	+ Highly customizable
	+ Low costs for large teams
	+ Community-driven development
* Cons:
	+ Requires technical expertise to set up
	+ Limited integration options
	+ May not be as user-friendly as Miro
	+ Limited customer support
	+ Still in active development, with some features missing

## When to Choose Each
Miro is a good choice for teams that prioritize ease of use, scalability, and integration with other tools. It's suitable for large teams and enterprises that need a reliable, cloud-based solution. On the other hand, Excalidraw is ideal for teams that value data ownership, customization, and cost-effectiveness. It's perfect for small to medium-sized teams, or those with technical expertise, who want a self-hosted solution with full control over their data.

Excalidraw is also a good choice for teams that are already familiar with open-source tools and are comfortable with manual configuration. Additionally, teams that require a high degree of customization and are willing to invest time in setting up and configuring Excalidraw may find it to be a good fit.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Miro boards in JSON format using the Miro API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up an Excalidraw server, either locally or on a cloud platform.
3. Use the Excalidraw import tool to import your Miro boards into Excalidraw.
4. Configure Excalidraw to match your team's workflow and customize as needed.
5. Test and verify that all data has been migrated correctly.

## Our Take
Excalidraw is still a relatively new tool, and while it shows great promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. It lacks some features and polish compared to Miro, and its self-hosting requirement can be a barrier for non-technical teams. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Excalidraw's collaboration features are still in development, and real-time co-editing is not yet available. Despite these limitations, Excalidraw is a great choice for teams that value data ownership and customization, and are willing to invest time in setting it up. Teams that are already using Miro and are looking for a more cost-effective solution may want to consider switching to Excalidraw.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need advanced integrations
* Technical teams who value data ownership and self-hosting
* Teams who are already using open-source tools and are comfortable with manual configuration
* Teams who require a high degree of customization and are willing to invest time in setting up Excalidraw
* Teams who are looking for a cost-effective solution and don't mind limited customer support

## FAQ

Yes, Excalidraw is free and open-source, and you can self-host it on your own server. However, you will need to pay for server costs.
### Is Excalidraw as user-friendly as Miro?
No, Excalidraw is still in active development, and its user interface may not be as polished as Miro's. However, it is still relatively easy to use, especially for technical teams.
### Can I integrate Excalidraw with other tools?
Yes, Excalidraw has some integration options, but they are limited compared to Miro. You may need to use third-party tools or APIs to integrate Excalidraw with other tools.
### Is Excalidraw suitable for large teams?
Excalidraw can be used by large teams, but it may require more manual configuration and technical expertise to set up and scale. Miro may be a better choice for very large teams.

Yes, you can export your Miro boards in JSON format and import them into Excalidraw using the Excalidraw import tool.

# Netlify vs Coolify (2026)

## Overview
Netlify and Coolify are two popular tools used for building, deploying, and managing web applications. This comparison is beneficial for developers, startups, and businesses looking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted solution. The core use case for both tools is to provide a seamless development experience, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and infrastructure.

## Key Differences

* Data Ownership: Coolify allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Netlify stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup Complexity: Netlify has a more straightforward setup process, while Coolify requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Netlify provides automatic scaling, whereas Coolify requires manual configuration for scaling.
* Integration: Netlify has built-in support for GitHub and GitLab, while Coolify supports GitLab and requires additional setup for GitHub integration.

| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|----------|---------|

* Automatic scaling and performance optimization
* Built-in support for GitHub and GitLab
* Free plan available with limited features
* Limited control over data and infrastructure
**Coolify:**
* Self-hosted and free
* Full control over data and infrastructure
* Customizable and extensible
* Apache 2.0 license
* Steeper learning curve and setup complexity

## When to Choose Each
Netlify is suitable for small to medium-sized teams and startups that prioritize ease of use and automatic scaling. It's ideal for teams that don't require full control over their data and infrastructure. Coolify, on the other hand, is suitable for larger teams, enterprises, and organizations that require full control over their data and infrastructure. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Coolify requires manual configuration for scaling, which can be time-consuming and error-prone. However, for teams that require full control over their data and infrastructure, Coolify is a viable alternative to Netlify, and we recommend switching to Coolify if you have the technical expertise and resources to support it.

* Medium-sized teams with 10-20 members that need full control over their data and infrastructure

### Can I migrate my Netlify site to Coolify?

No, Coolify is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires significant technical expertise to set up and configure.

title: Salesforce vs EspoCRM
comparison_markdown:
# Salesforce vs EspoCRM

## Overview

The world leading CRM platform. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. EspoCRM is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Salesforce costs $25-$300+/user/month; EspoCRM is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Salesforce is Proprietary; EspoCRM is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: EspoCRM can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: EspoCRM eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: EspoCRM has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Salesforce | EspoCRM |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$1,250/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$5,000/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Salesforce

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### EspoCRM

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [espocrm/espocrm](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm) * ~2k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Salesforce if:** Salesforce is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose EspoCRM if:** EspoCRM is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Salesforce in its standard export format, review EspoCRM import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

EspoCRM is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Salesforce tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your EspoCRM instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Salesforce, switching to self-hosted EspoCRM will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Salesforce until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Salesforce paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is EspoCRM free to use?
Yes. EspoCRM is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Salesforce to EspoCRM?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Salesforce data, follow the EspoCRM import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does EspoCRM get regular updates?
Yes. EspoCRM has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use EspoCRM without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if EspoCRM development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Salesforce](https://salesforce.com) and [EspoCRM](https://espocrm.com) before making decisions.*

# Sentry vs GlitchTip (2026)

## Overview
Sentry and GlitchTip are error tracking and monitoring tools designed to help developers identify and resolve issues in their applications. This comparison is beneficial for development teams seeking to optimize their error tracking workflow, particularly those considering switching from a proprietary solution to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is to provide real-time error tracking and alerts, with the key reason to switch being the desire for greater control over data ownership and costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Sentry offers a free plan with limited features, while GlitchTip is completely free and open-source, with optional self-hosting.
* Data ownership: GlitchTip allows for full data ownership, as users can self-host the platform, whereas Sentry stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Sentry has a more straightforward setup process, while GlitchTip requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Sentry is designed to handle large volumes of data and traffic, while GlitchTip's scalability depends on the user's self-hosting infrastructure.
* Integration with GitHub: Sentry has native integration with GitHub, while GlitchTip relies on third-party integrations or manual configuration.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Sentry | GlitchTip |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $26-$80+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | BSD |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $26-$40/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $80-$160/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Sentry:**
* Easy setup and integration with popular frameworks
* Robust feature set, including real-time error tracking and alerts
* Scalable and reliable infrastructure
* Native integration with GitHub and other development tools
* Limited free plan features
**GlitchTip:**
* Completely free and open-source
* Self-hosting option for full data ownership
* Customizable and extensible through third-party integrations
* Limited native integrations with popular frameworks
* Requires technical expertise for self-hosting

## When to Choose Each
Sentry is ideal for large development teams or enterprises that require a scalable, reliable error tracking solution with native integrations with popular frameworks. Its robust feature set and straightforward setup process make it a good choice for teams that prioritize ease of use and don't mind the costs associated with a proprietary solution. On the other hand, GlitchTip is suitable for small to medium-sized development teams or individuals who value data ownership and customization. Its self-hosting option and open-source nature make it an attractive choice for teams with limited budgets or specific technical requirements.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Sentry data in JSON format using the Sentry API or the built-in export tool.
2. Set up a GlitchTip instance, either by self-hosting or using a third-party hosting service.
3. Use the GlitchTip import tool to migrate your exported Sentry data into your new GlitchTip instance.
4. Configure your GlitchTip instance to integrate with your development tools and frameworks.
5. Test your GlitchTip setup to ensure that error tracking and alerts are working as expected.

## Our Take
GlitchTip is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the features and polish of more established error tracking solutions like Sentry. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that GlitchTip's self-hosting infrastructure can be complex to set up and manage, particularly for teams without extensive technical expertise. However, for small to medium-sized development teams or individuals who value data ownership and customization, GlitchTip is a viable alternative to Sentry, and we recommend considering it as an option.

## Who Should Switch
* Small development teams (less than 10 members) who don't need native GitHub integration
* Individuals or solo developers who prioritize data ownership and customization
* Teams with limited budgets who can't afford Sentry's proprietary costs
* Development teams with specific technical requirements that aren't met by Sentry's features
* Open-source projects that require a free, self-hosted error tracking solution

## FAQ
### Is GlitchTip completely free?
Yes, GlitchTip is completely free and open-source, with optional self-hosting.
### Can I self-host Sentry?
No, Sentry does not offer self-hosting options.
### Is GlitchTip production-ready?
Not yet, as it still lacks some features and polish compared to more established error tracking solutions.
### Can I migrate my Sentry data to GlitchTip?
Yes, you can export your Sentry data in JSON format and import it into GlitchTip using the built-in import tool.
### Does GlitchTip have native integration with GitHub?
No, GlitchTip relies on third-party integrations or manual configuration for GitHub integration.
